results.content: DexVLG is evaluated against diffusion-based small baselines (DGN2.0 variants) in simulation benchmarks covering seen and unseen objects, showing superior simulation success rates and part grasp accuracy for both part-conditioned and contact mode-conditioned instruction generation, while remaining robust to novel objects and alternative part segmentation methods. The results indicate that large vision-language models are necessary for instruction-aligned dexterous grasping, since augmenting the small baseline with CLIP text features improves language alignment but degrades grasp quality. Ablation studies reveal that training data scale and color input are critical for performance, while model size beyond a mid-sized backbone yields only marginal gains. Real-world tests with a ShadowHand [...] DexVLG consistently outperforms DGN2.0-based baselines across all simulation benchmarks, achieving higher success rates and part accuracy. It also shows robust generalization to unseen objects and alternative part segmentation methods. DexVLG achieves notably higher simulation success and part grasp accuracy than DGN2.0+CLIP on every benchmark. On unseen objects, DexVLG retains 79% success rate and 36% part grasp accuracy, demonstrating strong generalization. Using SamPart3D segmentation, DexVLG maintains high performance with 76% success and 52% part accuracy. Adding CLIP features to DGN2.0 improves language alignment but reduces success rate, indicating small model capacity limits. [...] The experiments evaluate the DexVLG model against established baselines using simulation benchmarks that assess success rate, part-level grasp accuracy, and generalization to unseen objects and segmentation methods. DexVLG consistently surpasses DGN2.0-based approaches, demonstrating robust performance even with alternative part segmentation, while adding CLIP features to baselines improves language alignment but degrades success due to capacity limits. Incorporating contact mode labels strongly enhances instruction-following grasp generation, especially for part-level compliance, and explicit language instruction boosts success across all benchmarks with the greatest gains on unseen objects, confirming its necessity for part-aware evaluation. Each grasp pose is mapped to semantic parts of the object and paired with detailed part-level captions describing the grasped part and style. The dataset is generated using a physics-based simulation pipeline and validated in Isaac Gym to ensure physical plausibility.

# [Literature Review] DexVLG: Dexterous Vision-Language-Grasp Model at Scale

This paper presents DexVLG, a large Vision-Language-Grasp model designed for predicting dexterous grasp poses aligned with language instructions using single-view RGBD input. The core contributions are the creation of a large-scale synthetic dataset, DexGraspNet 3.0, and the development of the DexVLG model trained on this dataset. Our extensive experiments demonstrate DexVLG's great zero-shot generalizability, achieving over 76\% zero-shot execution success rate and state-of-the art part grasp accuracy in simulation, and demonstrate successful part-aligned grasps on real-world objects. [...] As large models begin to gain momentum, vision-language foundation models are enabling robots to generalizably perform more and more tasks. However, due to the difficulty in data collection, the benefits are limited with simple embodiments. In this paper, we present \textbf{DexVLG}, a vision-language model that predicts language instruction-aligned dexterous grasp poses given single-view RGBD perception. To achieve this, we first synthesize a dataset of 170M dexterous grasp poses aligned with semantic parts on 174k objects in simulation, paired with informative part-level captions. With this large-scale dataset named \textbf{DexGraspNet 3.0}, we train a flow-matching VLM to generate instruction-aligned grasp poses on tabletop objects.
